chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the room is above eight cubits, write in its upper part the Verse of the Chair.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inscribing Quranic verses in rooms with specific heights?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking architectural dimensions to spiritual protection, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating faith into daily domestic life. The specific threshold of eight cubits (*adru'*) likely corresponds to the minimum height for a habitable space, ensuring that significant living areas are consecrated through the recitation or inscription of Ayat al-Kursi. This practice underscores the belief in the protective power of divine words within the home, a concept deeply rooted in both Quranic exegesis and popular Shia piety.
